Technically, an OHP with your heels together is a genuine military press. You can't wrangle as much weight with that stance, but it is better at building core strength.

When your feet are shoulder width apart during an overhead press, the "balancing the load" aspect of the lift is distributed more evenly between the two legs. When your legs are together, the force vector is redirected to energize more of your abdominal stablizers, spinal erectors, etc. Think about how more wobbly you feel when you lift a heavy object over your head with feet drawn together. To combat the wobble, you need to contract the stablizers running up and down your torso.

The stance isn't wrong, per se. As long as your spine remains aligned correctly throughout the lift, your foot position isn't going to wreck you, provided you can control the load.

Well... to be fair, all it takes is a bit of intelligence and a bit of research to recognize the inherent danger of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac.

Fannie Mae came about after the Great Depression. The federal government was trying to get banks to take part in a secondary market in debt, in order to create (the illusion of) more capital in order to (appear to) expand the economy. The banks weren't interested in doing so, since they rightly saw investments in existing debt to be a poor risk, with little return and too much chance for loss. So the federal government created an agency to underwrite that risk and make it such that the banks would take part in the desired secondary market.

It was such a bust that in 1968, it was spun off into a quasi-private company, specifically in order to remove its debt and ongoing losses from the federal budget.

But not surprisingly (and arguably by design) it turned out to be a boon for the biggest banks, since it created a situation of moral hazard - that is, a situation in which the banks could invest in the secondary marke and know that they were free to keep any profits and that any losses would be covered by the taxpayers.

But also not surprisingly, that situation of moral hazard did what they tend to do - it led to rampant abuse by those who were shielded from loss at the expense of those who were not.
